michelle_support: FYI customer running a nightly bulk embed job (~1.2M rows). Starting ~00:30 UTC they hit repeated 429s and some downstream errors 'Dimension mismatch'. They say it used to work last week. Need triage and guidance.
aj_ops: can you paste sample request ids + which model and batch size? also any client-side parallelism?
michelle_support: model: open-embed-1536 (customer believes 1536-dim). They send batch_size=128, concurrency=16 from their farm. Example request id: r-8f3a2b. Log shows 429 spike ~00:45:
```
status=429 msg="Too Many Requests" code=429 request_id=r-8f3a2b retry_after=3 headers="x-rate-limit-remaining:0; x-retry-after:3; x-rate-limit-limit:60"
```
Also saw an error in pipeline: "Dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024" for some vectors.
sre-bot: automated alert: embeddings-rate-limit burst_exceeded window=60s count=130
lina_eng: two likely issues here: 1) true 429s from hitting burst/concurrency limits, 2) the dimension errors mean some consumers are expecting a different model or truncated vectors. They may be mixing model versions or a post-processing step is downsampling.
aj_ops: ask customer to run a focused repro: single-threaded curl loop with batch_size=1 to confirm model dims and isolate rate limits. Example:
```
for i in {1..10}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":"test-$i"}' | jq .; 
  sleep 0.2
done
```
If that returns 1536-dim vectors consistently, we can rule out model mismatch.
michelle_support: customer ran single-threaded, vectors show 1536 dims consistently. They only see 1024 vectors when running their bulk pipeline under high concurrency.
lina_eng: that points to a client-side batching/packing bug. Possible causes: their client is reusing a different model key for some batches, or an internal compression/quantization step kicks in under memory pressure. Also their concurrency 16 * batch 128 = 2048 items in flight — that will trigger burst quota. Our burst config allows short spikes but sustained concurrency over the per-account QPS will 429.
aj_ops: immediate mitigations to suggest to customer: reduce concurrency to 4, drop batch_size to 64, add exponential backoff with jitter on 429s (base=0.5s, max=8s), and respect Retry-After header. Ask them to ramp traffic over 10 minutes instead of starting all at once.
michelle_support: relayed mitigations. Customer reports 429 rate dropped but some batches still show 1024-dim.
lina_eng: ask them to log the model name and API key per request at client side. Also check any intermediate queue/worker that might be hitting a legacy env var (e.g., EMBED_MODEL=embed-1024).
customer-team: confirmed: one worker process had an old env var EMBED_MODEL=open-embed-1024 — that explains inconsistent dims. We missed it in deploy. Sorry.
aj_ops: great find. For long-term stability: offer them two options — a) move large nightly job to Dedicated capacity (reserved throughput) or b) implement client-side concurrency limiting and intelligent batching (we can share a sample backoff + concurrency library).
michelle_support: customer asked about quota increase to reduce 429s during ramp. What's our policy?
aj_ops: for production bulk jobs we can offer a temporary burst uplift if they schedule it and provide job plan. File a support request to infra-quota with the job window, expected QPS, and request_ids. We'll need approval.
sre-bot: note: quota uplift request template: team, project, timeframe, peak QPS, avg QPS, dataset size, contact.
lina_eng: add reproducible steps for us if they re-hit: 1) collect top 10 request_ids around a 429 window, 2) capture full client logs showing model param and batch payload sizes, 3) include HTTP response headers for a sample 429 (x-rate-limit-remaining, x-retry-after, x-rate-limit-limit), 4) if dimension errors occur capture the raw returned vector length and the expected length.
michelle_support: I'll gather logs + request ids and open infra-quota ticket with a proposed uplift window (2 hours next Wednesday night). Customer agreed to throttle for now.
customer-team: thanks — we'll also rotate workers to ensure env parity before next run.
aj_ops: follow-up items for us: (1) check account's current burst quota and recent spike graph in console, (2) pre-approve uplift if traffic plan looks safe, (3) share the concurrency/backoff snippet with customer.
lina_eng: small note: we should consider adding a quick client-side sanity check lib we can publish — returns expected vector length for active model to catch env mismatch early. I'll open an internal ticket.
michelle_support: marking this thread resolved for now, will reopen if we get more 429s after mitigations. :white_check_mark:
aj_ops: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
